methods.text: not available for Kentucky: KYTC prices crashes with the National Safety Council's comprehensive costs (KYTC HSIP reports 2023-2025, benefit/cost lines) and publishes no table of its own; and the public data has no A/B/C level, so only K and O could be priced and a cost total would be misleading

not available for Kentucky: KTC publishes statewide average and critical crash rates per 100 MVM by highway type (Analysis of Traffic Crash Data in Kentucky 2020-2024, rate tables after p. ix), but CrashIQ has no Kentucky traffic counts to apply them

Highway Safety Manual (AASHTO, 1st, 2010), Ch. 4, Sec. 4.2.3. Kentucky's own method, KYTC ranks HSIP sites by the cost of excess expected crashes (KTC SPFs + Empirical Bayes, KA/B/C/O); KTC's high-crash-location critical rate uses K = 2.576 (p = 0.995), Cc = Ca + K*sqrt(Ca/M) + 1/(2M) (KTC 2020-2024, p. ix, PDF p. 11), isn't built: this report uses the HSM critical rate against the corridor's own sites (national method)
not available for Kentucky: KTC's analysis and KYTC's screening use five years of crashes (KTC 2020-2024, Table 1, PDF p. 20) but set no minimum study period for a corridor study
